about.title: Westlake Village Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Westlake Village is a small city, but its roads still see a steady stream of injury collisions — 27 reported in the most recent final year, with 39 people hurt. Corridors like Lindero Canyon Road, Agoura Road, Thousand Oaks Boulevard, and Triunfo Canyon Road carry much of that traffic, and Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to see more reported crashes than other times. If you were injured in one of these collisions, what happens in the days right after matters. Photos, witness contacts, and vehicle damage can disappear or fade from memory quickly. Our team handles personal injury claims for Westlake Village residents and visitors, starting with evidence gathering and dealing with insurers, so you're not doing it alone while trying to recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. We can help make sure that deadline — whichever applies — doesn't slip by.

items.title: Pure Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces what you can collect. We can push back on inflated fault percentages the other insurer may try to assign you.

items.title: Recorded Statements Aren't Required — and Rarely Help You
items.desc: You're not obligated to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and doing so early on can be used against you later. Letting us handle that communication protects what you say from being twisted.

items.question: Do I have to give a statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: No, you're not required to give a recorded statement to the other side's insurer. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can minimize your claim, even if it doesn't feel that way in the moment. It's usually safer to let us communicate with them on your behalf.

items.question: What if the crash happened on a road maintained by the city or county?
items.answer: Claims involving government-maintained roads or intersections can carry much shorter deadlines — sometimes as little as six months to file a claim notice. Given how many of Westlake Village's reported crashes cluster around corridors like Agoura Road and Thousand Oaks Boulevard, it's worth having an attorney check quickly whether a government entity might be involved.

items.question: How do you get paid?
items.answer: We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid a fee if you recover compensation. There's no cost to you upfront.
